description: Compose ANY edit or transition yourself; there is no preset list. Segments on an output timeline (later ones drawn on top; overlapping ones ARE the transition), each animated by keyframes (scale, x, y, rotate, opacity, blur, mblur, exposure, speed ramps, holds, reverse), plus your own HTML overlays and masks, compiled server-side into one render. Whip pan, zoom through, push, spin, slow motion, freeze frame, J-cut / L-cut, wipes, split screen, picture in picture: all composed from the fields. Local render at the flat post_edit price (~2 credits, overlays included); a `generate` segment (a paid generated transition shot) only when the user explicitly asks. SOURCES: src is 'this' (videoUrl), a Library / render URL, a direct file or a PUBLIC TikTok / Reel / Facebook / X post link (a YouTube link is refused up front, free: YouTube does not let us download videos, so upload the file). in/out are SOURCE seconds; out:'payoff' cuts just before a hook's payoff. Every seam is matched automatically (grade, level, grain) and the reply carries a vision REVIEW of each seam (pro / ok / amateur, with fixes) plus the seam frames; when it says ok or amateur, fix what it names and re-run with the same sources (twice at most) before presenting. video_frames shows exact frames free: look before you cut, and check the result. Follow-ups ('cut earlier', 'whip pan instead') re-run with the same sources and the one change. Refusals are free and name the field. READ THE MANUAL FIRST: call get_skill('hermoso-edit-timeline') before composing. It holds the transition recipes with their exact keyframes (whip pan, zoom through, push, spin, speed ramp, freeze, wipes, split screen), how to link two unrelated clips with a match cut, the viral-hook-plus-product method, audio payoff and L/J-cut rules, and the pro-not-iMovie checklist.

expected_credits.description: the get_cost price; refused unbilled if the live price differs

fps.description: the frame rate, a whole number from 24 to 60 (24, 25, 30, 60 are the usual ones). Leave it out: the canvas takes the rate of its own footage (the rate of most of it on screen), so no frames are invented; a faster clip is thinned, a slower one that does not divide it is motion-interpolated

get_cost.description: true: return the price only; nothing runs or bills

idempotency_key.description: chosen once, resent unchanged on retries: the same key never buys twice

motionBlur.description: default true: anything that moves gets a real shutter blur along its path

overlays.description: HTML/CSS overlays animated with @keyframes, each shown between its start and end

html.description: HTML/CSS animated with @keyframes; no script, no network (images as data: URIs)

mode.description: 'mask': its opaque pixels are where `segment` shows

segment.description: for mode mask: 0-based index of the segment whose opaque shape it reveals

review.description: default true: a vision read of each seam (about 2 credits) comes back with the render, with the seam frames

segments.description: the clips on the output, max 12, later ones on top. Every animated field (scale x y rotate opacity exposure blur mblur brightness contrast saturation, audio.gain) is a constant or keyframes [{t: seconds into this segment | src: a second of the source, v, ease: linear|in|out|inout|hold}]; x and y are in canvas widths / heights, rotate in degrees, mblur in px along mblurAngle

anchor.description: canvas point (0-1) that stays put while it scales

x.description: canvas x, 0 to 1, that stays put while the segment scales

y.description: canvas y, 0 to 1, that stays put while the segment scales

at.description: output second it starts (default: right after the previous)

audio.description: this segment's sound: mute, gain, lead, tail, fades and level

fadeIn.description: fade-in length in seconds for this segment's sound

fadeOut.description: fade-out length in seconds for this segment's sound

lead.description: seconds its sound starts before its picture (a J-cut)

level.description: match levels its loudness to the clips around it; keep leaves it as recorded

tail.description: seconds its sound runs past the cut (an L-cut), or payoff for the hook's own payoff sound

between.description: a bridge clip between its neighbours (a re-used generated shot): trimmed and graded to them automatically

blur.description: constant or keyframes [{t or src, v, ease}]

contrast.description: constant or keyframes [{t or src, v, ease}]

crop.description: fractions of the source frame, or 'auto': the picture only, without letterbox bars and their caption

exposure.description: × the light, 1 = as shot (a fine grade)

fit.description: how the picture fills the canvas: auto, fill, contain or blur

generate.description: PAID: a new shot between its neighbours

model.description: a model id that takes start AND end frames

prompt.description: description of a generated transition shot (paid; only when the user asks)

seconds.description: how long to hold that frame, in seconds

src.description: source second of the frame to freeze

match.description: the cut INTO this segment (default: the timeline match)

mblurAngle.description: motion blur direction in degrees, used with mblur

opacity.description: constant or keyframes [{t or src, v, ease}]

out.description: source second to stop at, or 'payoff' (default: the end)

overlap.description: seconds it starts before the previous ends: the transition window

radius.description: rounded corners, a fraction of the picture's shorter side (0-0.5): a picture-in-picture CARD over the segment under it, any length

reverse.description: true plays the segment backwards at one constant speed, with no holds

saturation.description: constant or keyframes [{t or src, v, ease}]

scale.description: constant or keyframes [{t or src, v, ease}]

slowmo.description: how slow motion fills frames (flow = motion-interpolated)

speed.description: 0.05-8, or a ramp over source seconds

src.description: 'this' or a video URL / public post link

sfx.description: sound effects placed on the output timeline

gain.description: level in dB, -30 to 6; omit to match the sound under it

segment.description: payoff: the segment whose OWN payoff sound (the egg's real splat) lands at `at`

size.description: canvas: '9:16' default, '1:1', '4:5', '16:9', any 'W:H' (1:3 to 3:1, on a 1080 short side) or exact 'WxH' pixels

videoUrl.description: the video 'this' refers to (optional when every segment names its own src)

name: edit_timeline
title: Compose an edit (timeline)
